cases.summary: A non-run command stamps protocolVersion 2 and keeps its free-form payload in data.
A usage failure carries the taxonomy code in error.code and the matching exit code.
A successful plan-only JSON invocation reports a typed plan and no run because no session executed.
UNIFIED SUCCESS: a run whose tasks were served from cache is a success — reuse is provenance, counted apart in run.reuse, and never removes a task from the verdict histogram.
A Docker publish terminal result carries typed phase facts, an immutable digest, and distinct configured versus observed concurrency.
UNIFIED SUCCESS: the one failed task was a local cache hit and still fails the run. Version 1's lenient JSONL summary reported success here.

ABORT PRECEDENCE: an interrupted run reports status "aborted" with exit 130 on the envelope, exactly like the process — and the failures it did collect stay readable in run.counts.failed and run.failures.
A failing run may report a forwarded workload exit code; only 0 and 130 are reserved by the verdict.
A task:start record carries the typed identity and nothing else.
A workspace-once task is identified structurally by scope, not by a synthetic project name a reader has to recognize.
A task:event wraps one subprocess runtime event; the inner payload is versioned by protocols/runtime, not re-specified here.
Status and reuse are orthogonal: a restored failure keeps its verdict and its error instead of being presented as a cache hit with no outcome.
A plan-only JSONL invocation closes with plan:end even when the plan is empty; it never synthesizes a zero-task session.
The session:end record carries the same run summary the JSON envelope does — one verdict shape on every surface.
run_jobs returns the canonical run summary instead of its own count vocabulary.
plan_jobs reports planned tasks by typed identity; edges reference the derived keys.
The recorded session document is versioned and reports the canonical run summary in place of its own stats vocabulary.
A local request records local execution.
A remote request records remote execution.
With no execution provider, local fallback preserves the requested remote placement.
Unknown placement is omitted, never null.
Placement is an object, not a location string.
Both requested and actual placement are required when placement is known.
Only local and remote are valid placement values.
Null placement members cannot imply local or remote execution.
Placement does not accept producer-owned metadata.
A session recorded by the executing engine of a bound request states the source, execution-input and submission identities it ran for, in the runner contract's digest spelling.
Provenance is complete or absent: the executing engine states all three identities from one bound request.
Unknown provenance is omitted, never null.
Provenance digests carry the sha256: prefix and 32 lowercase hex characters name the submission, so a session identity compares with a request identity as one string.
A bound request executes only as the remote placement; provenance beside a local execution is a claim nothing executed.
Provenance names no attempt, provider or machine: those are transport observations and live beside the session.

The session names the worktree it ran against by CONTENT, so a later reader compares one string instead of recomputing a digest against a tree that may have moved since. dirty is stated even when it is false: the block is written only when the fingerprint was computed, and that one computation is what decides all three members.

The fingerprint is a join key two parties compare as strings, so it is the FULL lowercase hex sha256 and nothing else. An abbreviation, or the same digest in uppercase, reads as a different tree against every correctly spelled record — which is exactly the silent disagreement the member exists to remove.

A present tree block knows all three facts, because one computation produces them together. Absence of the WHOLE object — never of a member — is how a producer says it could not determine which tree it ran against.
The recorded plan snapshot is versioned and carries typed identities.
A stream line must be one JSON value; trailing data is not a second document.
Every v2 document is a JSON object.
A version 1 envelope is not a version 2 document: the stamp is what tells the two apart.
protocolVersion is exact, never a floor.
Documents are closed: an undeclared member is drift, not an extension point.
Member types are exact; a number where a string belongs is drift, not coercion.
A preview plan cannot claim that a run executed in the same envelope.
A preview envelope exposes its typed plan directly and cannot carry an unrelated data payload.
A successful preview plan cannot simultaneously report an error.
A plan member is the terminal fact of a completed preview and therefore requires status success with exit code zero.
A preview cannot claim non-empty work when its typed task list is empty.
A successful document carries no error member.
A Docker terminal fact never accepts a mutable tag where immutable digest provenance is required.
A failed document must name its failure.
ABORT PRECEDENCE: an aborted envelope reporting 1 is exactly the version 1 disagreement with the process, which returns 130.
130 belongs to an abort; a genuine failure may not claim it.
The error class and the verdict are one decision: only an aborted document carries "signal".
Symmetric to the case above: a failure document may not borrow the signal class.
The envelope and its run summary are one verdict: their exit codes cannot differ.
ABORT PRECEDENCE: the version 1 JSON envelope reported an interrupted run that also had failures as a plain failure. Version 2 rejects it — the abort source without the aborted outcome is the drift.
UNIFIED SUCCESS: version 1's session:end summary called this run green because the failing task was a cache hit. Version 2 rejects the verdict.
The verdict is derived, not asserted: a failure outcome needs a failed task.
counts.total is the sum of the four verdict buckets over every selected task.
The reuse histogram spans the same task set as the verdict histogram, so it can never exceed it.
A listed failure set is complete: counting two failures and naming one hides the reused half of the run.
An aborted run names its source, so an operator can tell a Ctrl-C from a supervisor's SIGTERM.
An interrupted run is never green: 130, never 0.
TYPED IDENTITY: key is a projection of project.id and task.name, never an independent value.
TYPED IDENTITY: the providing extension is part of the identity, not optional metadata.
TYPED IDENTITY: identity is structured fields only — a display-name member has nowhere to live.
Scope is a closed vocabulary.
A record variant's member set is exact, so a reader can switch on `record` alone.
A task:end record without its terminal result is not a terminal record.
Only session:end carries a run verdict; a per-task record cannot claim one.
A succeeded task carries no error.
Durations are non-negative integer milliseconds.
Diagnostic severities are a closed vocabulary shared with the diagnostic protocol.
A tool result carries the member its tool produces and no other.
A plan:end record cannot claim an executed run and must carry the typed plan it completed.
plan_jobs must return a plan.

One physical execution carries the measured rusage for the whole batch; both logical records reference it by id, a reused task references none, and a superseded attempt stays in the ledger with tasks 0 because the machine still paid for it.

A run a task spawned names its parent session and the selection it planned over, so an accounting consumer can tell a gate from the nested run it charged and read the selection without guessing it from the project list.

A session that published beside its gate records both halves: projects is the union the run planned and executed, and releaseSetProjects is the subset whose publish and package steps the release-set plan owned, so a consumer never attributes a publication to the gate selection or a verification to the channel head.

A whole-workspace run records mode all and scoped false; a session that carries neither selection nor parent is a top-level run over an unstated selection, which every record written before the members existed is.
The selection mode is a closed vocabulary; a spelling outside it would let a consumer silently classify a run it cannot classify.
A session cannot be its own parent; the shape means the producer stamped the ambient parent id beside its own, and a consumer trusting it would drop the top-level run out of its ledger.
A task's executionId must name an execution the same document declares; a dangling reference drops that task's cost from the physical roll-up.

Every record that was keyed names the cache key it was keyed on: an executed task, a reused one and a replayed failure each carry an inputDigest, and the skipped dependent carries none because it never looked a key up.
inputDigest uses the sha256: spelling every digest on the wire uses; the bare hex the store addresses entries by would not compare with any other digest as one string.
A skipped task never looked its key up, so a digest beside it names inputs nothing was keyed on and a reader grouping records by digest would count a task that never ran.
A quota-limited Linux runner records stable memory capacity with provenance, closing cgroup v2 gauges, complete windowed memory.events and cgroup-scoped PSI without changing process maxRSS semantics.
A degraded capture omits unsupported cgroup memory, memory capacity and PSI facts instead of fabricating zeros; the existing process CPU and maxRSS meanings remain unchanged.

A cgroup v1 runner reports only facts with exact shared semantics: finite capacity, closing current usage, cgroup-lifetime peak and separately host-scoped PSI; v1 failcnt is not relabelled as a v2 event.
Cgroup v1 memory.stat and failcnt are not accepted under cgroup v2 composition and memory.events names, because similarly named counters with different semantics are worse than absent facts.
allocatedMs is allocatedMillicores applied over the SAME durationMs the summary states; publishing the two against different walls makes every utilization figure derived from them wrong.
Steal and iowait are columns of the /proc/stat total over the same window, so neither can exceed it — a producer that mixed two windows would otherwise publish a steal share above 100%.

A quota of zero is not a measurement: v2 cpu.max says either a positive quota or "max", v1 cpu.cfs_quota_us says either a positive quota or -1, and both unlimited cases are spelled by OMITTING quotaUs rather than by writing a ceiling of nothing.

The dependency-preparation stage is decomposed into ownership phases. Four extension runtimes compiled concurrently, so generation sums to 14.8 s inside a 4.2 s stage — the gap between the phase sum and the stage wall IS the parallelism, which is why parallelism is a required member.

A warm content-addressed store re-runs nothing: the stage enters resolution, verification and the store's own mutation, and GENERATION IS ABSENT rather than present with zero — the same measured-never-derived rule the environment block follows.
At parallelism 1 the phase spans cannot overlap, so they must fit inside the stage's own wall. 15.4 s of non-overlapping work inside 4.2 s of wall is not a measurement any producer can make.
The phase list is a histogram over ownership classes, not a per-step log. A repeated class makes every ratio a reader computes wrong, with nothing else in the document to reveal it.

The ownership vocabulary is closed. A step that fits none of network/resolution/verification/generation/mutation is a step whose cost nobody can act on, so it is classified rather than given a sixth bucket.
A recorded session always records its verdict.
A dependency edge references a task key; the empty string is not one.
An integer member accepts any JSON number carrying an integral safe-range value (1.0, 1e0) — the JSON Schema integer rule, identical in both runtimes whatever the wire encoding.
Integer members are bounded to IEEE-754's safe range: a value a JavaScript consumer would silently round is rejected by both runtimes, not accepted by one.
Violations sort by byte/code-unit order, never locale order: 'Zfield' precedes 'afield' in both runtimes on any host.

The run's contracted bilan: one verdict, a per-command synthesis whose totals sum to the run's own, a bounded per-job list, and the typed cache and scheduler subsets a consumer would otherwise scrape out of the raw session.

ABSENT IS NOT ZERO: a fully cached MCP run measured no CPU, no coverage and no remote cache, so cpu, coverage, cpuMs, cache and scheduler are OMITTED rather than reported as zeros a consumer would read as measurements.

The report is CLOSED and its vocabulary is commands, not phases: a producer that adds a member — even one named for the concept this document deliberately did not adopt — is rejected rather than silently carried.
A report is written from a SETTLED run: endTime is required, so an unfinished run has no report rather than a report a consumer would file with an open interval.
Origin is a CLOSED vocabulary: an aggregator has to keep agent traffic apart from a human's, and a third spelling would silently become a fourth population.
git.sha is the join key a longitudinal consumer files the report under, so it must be a full object id: a symbolic reference can move, and two reports filed under "HEAD" describe different commits.
The report's verdict obeys the same exit-code agreement every other v2 surface does: a successful run reports 0, whatever the report would rather say.
The flattened job identity keeps the derived-key rule: key is exactly project + ":" + task, so the report joins to the session's task records on a value neither side can spell differently.
A truncated report still accounts for every selected task: len(jobs) + elidedJobs equals run.counts.total, so a three-task run carrying one job cannot claim it left none out.
The per-command list is a HISTOGRAM over root commands, not a per-task log: a repeated command means every ratio a reader computes from it is wrong, with nothing else in the document to reveal it.

Every selected task belongs to exactly one root command, so the per-command totals PARTITION the run: a sum that disagrees means the synthesis describes a different task set than its own verdict does.
Per-command CPU is the sum of fresh tasks' shares of their executions, so it can be LESS than the run's actual CPU — superseded attempts belong to the run's ledger and to no command — but never more.
The test counters are one measurement, not four numbers: total is passed + failed + skipped, so a report cannot publish a pass rate against a denominator nothing produced.
Coverage is a share in [0,100] at a declared granularity — the contract's one non-integer member, and the one place a wrong unit (a ratio, a count) would otherwise pass as a percentage.
When a producer states covered and total it has stated the measurement twice, and the two must agree: there cannot be more covered units than measured ones.
The per-job diagnostic bound is a CONTRACT clause: a consumer that accepts this document accepts a stated worst case, so a seventeenth diagnostic is rejected rather than quietly read.
A diagnostic message is bounded to 1024 UTF-8 bytes: the report carries an identifiable excerpt, and the untruncated text stays in the session it synthesizes.
Restores are a SUBSET of hits — a key the cache did not hold cannot have been materialized — so the reverse means the two counters came from different accountings.
A producer opts into bounded live output only by carrying the fixed policy, exact split elision counters, bounded terminal run projection, and retained full-detail artifact.
The bounded profile is additive: a legacy session:end without machineOutput retains the original non-empty time contract instead of acquiring the bounded terminal's byte ceiling.
The direct bounded-record validator rejects an isolated UTF-16 surrogate from raw JSON before Go and JavaScript decoders can assign it different string values.
The bounded terminal run is a distinct projection: even empty failures and publications arrays are forbidden so their worst-case size cannot become producer discretion.
A bounded terminal dispatches directly to streamRunSummary rather than first validating as the legacy RunSummary, so a shared arithmetic error is reported exactly once.
Changing run dispatch must preserve legacy field validation: an absent discriminator does not hide an independent arithmetic error inside the declared run member.
An elision cannot claim records without bytes or bytes without records; whole compact records make the pair jointly zero or jointly positive.
The normal mode is exactly 1 MiB and 1024 records; a producer cannot silently select a different cap while claiming the same mode.
A test:case record attributes one failed case to its task: the full name, the suite, the runner's duration, the bounded failure output and where the case is declared.

testCase.name: TestParse/empty
testCase.output:
parse_test.go:41: expected an error, got nil
[…]
FAIL

cases.summary: A passed case carries only its name, suite, status and duration; output, file and line are optional.
A skipped case may carry the runner's skip reason as its output.
task:end counts the test cases that have no test:case record, so a reader knows the records it read are not every case the task ran.
A test:case record without its case payload describes nothing.
A case status outside passed, failed and skipped is rejected, not mapped to the nearest word.
A passed case carries no output: passing transcripts stay out of the stream.
The output bound is 4096 UTF-8 BYTES, not code points: 1024 four-byte emoji plus one letter is 4097 bytes in 1025 code points and is rejected.
A case without a name cannot be told apart from its siblings; a producer drops it instead of guessing one.
Only a test:case record carries a case; a task:end that carries one is rejected.

testCase.name: TestParse/empty
testCase.output:
parse_test.go:41: expected an error, got nil
[…]
FAIL

cases.summary: A test:case record carries one case, never its task's terminal result.

testCase.name: TestParse/empty
testCase.output:
parse_test.go:41: expected an error, got nil
[…]
FAIL

cases.summary: A line locates a case only inside a named file.

testCase.name: TestParse/empty
testCase.output:
parse_test.go:41: expected an error, got nil
[…]
FAIL

cases.summary: outputTruncated describes an output that is present; without one it is rejected.
testCasesDropped is absent when nothing was dropped, so a zero is rejected.

streamCases.summary: The mandatory bounded session:end line is inside both the 1 MiB/1024 total and its dedicated 16 KiB/one-record reserve, with zero elision and an identical retained artifact.
A standalone plan:end is valid live preview output but never a persisted session stream; whole-session validation requires session:end and its artifact proof.
Normal live output suppresses a debug-level passing-test transcript while retaining it in the artifact and reporting its exact whole-record byte count as ordinary elision.

An oversized ordinary record is elided even though it would fit by borrowing unused failure capacity; the later error record remains live, artifact detail stays complete, and the exact ordinary bytes are reported.
Ordinary and failure-priority overflow are accounted independently as whole sanitized record counts and exact compact JSON-plus-LF bytes while the retained artifact keeps both records.
Verbose admits debug detail and uses the larger fixed live ceiling: the same 780338-byte record that normal suppresses fits verbose's ordinary partition without changing the run verdict.
The retained and live copies contain the sanitizer output: ANSI is gone, a forbidden control is U+FFFD, and a sensitive member value is the fixed redaction marker.
An isolated UTF-16 surrogate escape is rejected from the raw JSON spelling before Go can replace it and JavaScript can preserve it, giving both bindings one sanitization result.
Sensitive member names are normalized for lookup and their values must be the fixed redaction marker in both the complete artifact and live stream.
A missing counter is reported structurally once per final copy; whole-stream accounting does not add a derived elision mismatch when no integer was present to compare.
Legacy per-line session:end records remain valid documents, but whole-stream conformance is an opt-in bounded profile and therefore requires machineOutput in both live and retained final records.
A fitting ordinary record present in the complete artifact must be forwarded; omitting it while declaring zero elision is detectable from the whole sequence.
Sanitization happens before both persistence and emission, so an ANSI control in either copy is rejected at its exact string leaf.
A megabyte-scale ordinary record cannot cross the total or ordinary partition, and claiming it was emitted with zero elision disagrees with deterministic selection.

Normal live output treats every test:case as debug detail, whatever its status: it keeps them only in the artifact and counts their exact bytes as ordinary elision, while the failed task:end stays live in the failure reserve.
Verbose live output admits every test:case record into the ordinary partition, so the live copy equals the artifact with zero elision.
